newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan rebel leader says fight in south nearly over.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebel leader says fight in south nearly over.

text.p: Sudanese rebel leader John Garang said on Wednesday war in southern Sudan was almost over after rebels seized the main road north to the southern capital of Juba.
Garang, leader of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), was speaking at a news conference in the village of Loka on the main road north from the captured major town of Yei to Juba.
"For practical reasons I declare the war over. The fighting over the Yei road was the last bit of it," said Garang, adding the rebels had "liberated" most of Eastern and Western Equatoria regions.
He said rebels would seize Juba but declined to say when. Rebels said that Loka was some 40 km (25 miles) south of Juba.
Garang said in its offensive since last week the rebels had killed about 3,000 Sudanese government troops and militiamen and wounded or captured 1,000. He said the SPLA lost several hundred men.
He said the rebels captured 14 T-55 tanks and 17 howitzers and described the fighting for Yei, the biggest town in Western Equatoria region, as "vicious". It fell a week ago to the SPLA.

It was obvious to foreign journalists who flew into southern Sudan on Wednesday much of the road to Juba in Eastern Equatoria was firmly in rebel hands. Hundreds of rebels were seen along the highway.
There were also burned-out trucks and several government outposts which had been abandoned with weapons left inside.
In Nairobi, an SPLA spokesman said earlier on Wednesday the rebels had recaptured the town of Chali el-Fil near the border with Ethiopia from government forces which seized it at the weekend.
Sampson Kwaje said SPLA forces on Monday attacked and recaptured the southeastern town, shot down a helicopter gunship and seized arms and ammunition. He said the three-man helicopter crew died.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
Sudanese President Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir announced the government's seizure of Chali el-Fil on Sunday from the SPLA, which had captured it in a rebel offensive in January.
Khartoum said Ethiopian and Eritrean troops did most of the fighting for the rebels in their offensives since January. Both countries and Uganda have denied fighting alongside the rebels.
The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem Arabised north but has made significant gains in the east and south since January.
